newsitem.title: USA: US corp bonds spread firm, players eye new supply.
newsitem.headline: US corp bonds spread firm, players eye new supply.

text.p: U.S. high-grade corporate bonds were unchanged to a tad lower at midday tracking U.S. Treasuries in moderate trading, dealers said.
Spreads to U.S. Treasuries were unchanged across most maturities, dealers said.
"Secondary trading is moderate, spreads are firm...I think most of the focus has been on the new supply," one high-grade trader said.
So far on Thurdsay, two issuers have tapped the corporate bond primary market with a few others still expected, syndicate sources said.
"Issues are just flowing into the market," one syndicate source said. "The market is very favorable right now."
On Wednesday, Morgan Guaranty tapped the new issue market with $300 million in AA1/AAA rated two-year senior notes to yield 6.00 percent via JP Morgan Securities.

Coca-Cola Enterprises followed with $300 million in A3/AA-minus rated 40-year bonds to yield 6.717 percent or 22 basis points over Treasuries. The issue has a seven-year put option and was underwritten by Salomon Brothers.
Still on the calendar for new issues are Medpartners deal for about $300 to $400 million via Smith Barney, sources said.

In secondary new issue trading, Airtouch Communications' new seven-year percent paper was seen trading earlier at a spread of 54 to 53 basis points. The issue priced on Wednesday at 54 basis points, traders said.

"The market was very active in the morning, then it just died," said one trader. "Activity had been fast and furious all week but players are getting business squared away ahead of tomorrow's numbers."

Meanwhile, in secondary junk trading, Trump Castles 11-3/4 percent paper was a key gainer in Thursday's trading. The issue traded in roller coaster fashion as high as 105 bid and then down to 103 bid but was last quoted at 104 bid.
The 11.75 percent paper closed on Wednesday at 102-3/4 bid, traders said.
Trump AC bonds were up 1/4 at 99-1/8 bid, they added.
Ralphs Groceries 10.45 paper traded 1/4 higher at 101-7/8 bid and the grocer's 11.0 percent debt also gained 1/4 to trade at 100-7/8 bid, traders added.
Wireless debt stablized today after losing some ground on Wednesday. Nextel debt traded up 3/8 at 63-5/8 bid, 64-1/8 offer, while Sprint zeros were unchanged at 57-1/4 bid, 57-3/4 offer.
